brief: Bernstein argues data center construction has replaced power availability as the binding constraint on AI buildout. US grid interconnection delays pushed developers to behind-the-meter power (22% of construction, 40% of pipeline), then engines and fuel cells, and now to modularisation as the next time-to-power lever: moving work from field to factory cuts deployment time 30-60% and eases an MEP labour ceiling Bernstein puts at up to 35GW of US additions by 2030 against roughly double that implied demand. Beyond speed, the thesis is that modularisation shifts value: procurement consolidates from individual components to integrated modules, letting vertically integrated OEMs supply 80-90% of module content internally and driving a modeled ~3pp net share gain for the best-positioned players. Halving a 30-month deployment could unlock $0.9B/GW of incremental value, ~$0.2B/GW (25%) captured by OEMs. Bernstein rates Schneider, Vertiv and Eaton best positioned on positioning and execution, while Legrand, ABB and Siemens lag with narrower, less-integrated portfolios unless they integrate further.
